claims.location: source name all rows
claims.value: <MaxQuant experiment> orthograft tumour (light); super-SILAC standard aliquot spiked into <experiment> (heavy)
claims.evidence: 18 tumours = MaxQuant experiments CWR_1-3, 22RV1_1-3, LNCAP_1-3, LNCAPAI_1-3, VCAP_1-3, VCAPCR_1-3 (21 fractions each; mqpar and summary.txt agree, every raw stem maps to one experiment). iScience: "Triplicates were used for each HN and CR model resulting in 18 tumours". Each tumour lysate "mixed at 1:1 ratio with the super-SILAC standard prior to FASP". The heavy source names are 18 aliquots of ONE physical super-SILAC standard pool (one name per tumour mixture, as required for a shared reference).

claims.location: comment[label] all rows
claims.value: SILAC light = tumour lysate; SILAC heavy = super-SILAC standard
claims.evidence: iScience SILAC standard development: standard cell lines grown in RPMI with "heavy labelled SILAC amino acid ... Arginine (Arg10) ... Lysine (Lys8)"; "Column means of normalised Light / Heavy SILAC ratio were generated as a measure of the increase in abundance of protein in the CRPC model". mqpar labelMods = ["" (light), "Arg10;Lys8" (heavy)]; summary.txt Multiplicity 2, Labels1 Arg10;Lys8 on all 378 runs. Data check: mouse-only protein groups (host stroma; the standard is pure human cell culture) carry 87.5-95.0% of their intensity in L in every one of the 18 experiments, human-only groups are split L/H; SLFN5 log2 L/H CRPC minus HN = +1.4 (22RV1 vs CWR), +1.6 (LNCAPAI vs LNCAP; iScience reports 1.58), +1.15 (VCAPCR vs VCAP; iScience 1.05); AR strongly up in VCAPCR (+3.2 vs -0.2), as the preprint states (Fig 1d). Light = tumour confirmed.

limitations: Scope: PART 1 (PXD021428) only. PART 2 = PXD021405 (published 2022-10-14, linked to Cancer Res 2021), a separate label-free experiment (SLFN5 KO vs SCR orthografts, run names 20190308_SEL_LU_SA_RAM_..._KO1/KO11/SCR_...) - not annotated here, not the same experiment split across deposits.

Published Cancer Res article (doi:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-20-3694, no PMC) was not retrievable (publisher 403; bioRxiv JATS returned Cloudflare error 1015; not bypassed). The Research Square preprint (same title/authors) and the open iScience paper (PRIDE reference, same 18 tumours) were used.

CWR22Res has no Cellosaurus entry: cellosaurus accession/name = not available. iScience lists RRID CVCL_LI38 (CWR22Pc) for "CWR" - not used because CWR22Pc is a different named derivative and the same RRID list gives CVCL_4783 (LNCaP C4) for LNCaP, contradicting ATCC CRL-1740 (= LNCaP clone FGC, CVCL_1379) stated in the preprint.
VCAPCR tumours are annotated as cell line VCaP grown in castrated hosts (preprint: VCaP injected into both uncastrated and castrated mice); no in-vitro VCaP-CR line is described.
characteristics[organism part] = prostate (orthotopic tumour site). Cell-line origin sites differ (LNCaP: left supraclavicular lymph node; VCaP: vertebral bone metastasis; CWR22: primary prostate).
Tumour tissue contains mouse host stroma (organism annotated Homo sapiens; host in characteristics[xenograft]; search included mouse proteome).

experimentalDesignTemplate.txt is internally inconsistent: for each of the 18 samples the f021 file is assigned to a different experiment (cyclic off-by-one). mqpar.xml and summary.txt (the search actually run) assign all 21 fractions of each raw stem to one experiment; the SDRF follows mqpar/summary and raw names.
Runs deposited as .zip archives each wrapping one .raw; comment[data file] uses the .raw name (as searched).
Age not available for CWR22Res/22Rv1 (Cellosaurus "Adult" only). Passage number, cell type, storage temperature not reported.
parse_sdrf convert-openms reads only the first cleavage agent column.
Review: REVIEW_PENDING_EXTERNAL (no self-approval; no review-gate approve run).
